name: Creality Falcon A1 10W
tagline: Creality's compact enclosed A1: beginner-friendly diode in a small footprint
tldr: Creality Falcon A1 10W packs a diode engraver into an enclosed desktop body with Creality's software ecosystem. Less power than Falcon 2 Pro, but easier to live with in small spaces.
mainObjective: High-quality hobby and light-business engraving with light, slow cutting

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Arrives fully assembled, with a built-in HD camera for placing designs on objects
Class 1 enclosure: no goggles needed in normal use, and the laser stops when the lid opens
Lowest price of the A1 family ($549 on Creality's store, October 2026)
cons: Cutting is limited to thin wood and about 5 mm dark acrylic
Fills are slow at this power: about 12–18 min for a 10 × 10 cm photo in our benchmark
The enclosure contains smoke but does not remove it: an exhaust hose or purifier is still needed
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 10W SKU on Creality Falcon A1. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Run material test grids at engraving speeds first. Add air assist for light cuts. If cut jobs exceed ~30% of your week, open the higher-watt profile on this site and compare times.

editorialDepth.advantages: Creality Falcon A1 10W suits makers who sell marks, photos, and gifts more than daily panel cutting. Enclosed format is easier to live with at home.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if you already quote 4 mm+ cutting in production: see 20W in the line. Not for cast acrylic or bare metal without spray.

faq.question: What can the Falcon A1 10W cut?
faq.answer: Retailer spec sheets list about 5–6 mm basswood and around 5 mm black acrylic in one pass. Our materials list is more cautious and treats thin basswood in several passes as the comfortable range. A 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood took about 6–11 min in our benchmark.

faq.question: Falcon A1 10W or A1 Pro 20W?
faq.answer: The A1 10W ($549 on Creality's store, October 2026) suits engraving gifts, with the built-in camera for placement. The A1 Pro ($1,099) doubles the diode power, adds a 2W infrared laser for bare metal and plastics, and cuts about 10 mm basswood per Creality's spec. Pay the $550 difference only for metal marking or regular thick cuts.

faq.question: Bare unit, Basic kit or All-in-One kit?
faq.answer: In October 2026 Creality listed the bare A1 10W at $549, the Basic kit at $599 and the All-in-One kit at $699. The kits add accessories whose contents vary by listing, so compare them with what you already own (exhaust, air purifier, materials) before paying the extra $50–$150.

standoutFeatures.title: Camera placement out of the box
standoutFeatures.body: The built-in HD camera previews the bed, so you drag the design onto the object on screen instead of framing it by hand.

standoutFeatures.title: Assembled and Class 1
standoutFeatures.body: The A1 ships pre-assembled in a closed Class 1 body with a lid interlock, which makes it one of the simplest ways to start engraving safely indoors.
